package.name: python-3.15
package.description: the Python programming language (metapackage) (Werewolf fixed hardening policy)

vars.config-opts-jit: CC=clang-__llvm_version__ CFLAGS_JIT="$(if [ "$(uname -m)" = aarch64 ]; then echo -mbranch-protection=none; else echo -Os; fi)" --enable-experimental-jit=yes --with-tail-call-interp

pipeline.name: Fetch the locked source commit
pipeline.runs:
git init -q .
for delay in 0 15 45; do
  sleep "$delay"
  for source in https://github.com/python/cpython.git; do
    if git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c fetch.fsckObjects=true fetch --no-tags --depth=1 "$source" a73827e5bc4bb993504d5384071a8c734b36e2ea; then
      test "$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)" = a73827e5bc4bb993504d5384071a8c734b36e2ea
      git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout -q --detach a73827e5bc4bb993504d5384071a8c734b36e2ea
      exit 0
    fi
  done
done
echo "a73827e5bc4bb993504d5384071a8c734b36e2ea: every source failed, three times" >&2
exit 1

pipeline.name: Drop the branch development marker from the version string
pipeline.runs:
# Upstream sets PY_VERSION to "X.Y.Z+" on the maintenance branch as soon
# as X.Y.Z is tagged ("X.Y.Z+dev" on 3.15), and "X.Y.Z+" is not a valid
# PEP 440 version.
sed -i 's/^\(#define PY_VERSION[[:space:]]*"${{vars.upstreamversion}}\)+[a-z]*"/\1"/' Include/patchlevel.h
grep -q '^#define PY_VERSION[[:space:]]*"${{vars.upstreamversion}}"' Include/patchlevel.h

pipeline.name: Block blake and hmac usage in FIPS mode
Apply Werewolf policy patches
pipeline.runs:
while IFS= read -r name; do
  patch -p1 --forward --batch --fuzz=2 --no-backup-if-mismatch -i "werewolf/patches/$name" || exit 1
done < werewolf/patches/series

pipeline.name: Allow every runtime-hardening group in the build guest only
pipeline.runs:
mkdir -p /etc/runtime-hardening
: > /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
chmod 600 /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
mkdir -p /etc/runtime-hardening/allow/all/python
for f in native deserialize inline writable-source environment; do
  : > /etc/runtime-hardening/allow/all/python/$f
done

subpackages.name: ${{package.name}}${{range.key}}-runtime
subpackages.description: ${{package.name}}${{range.key}} with the python, python3 and pydoc3 commands

pipeline.runs:
find ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib -type f -name 'libpython*.a' -exec rm -rf '{}' +
find ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib -type d -name 'test' -exec rm -rf '{}' +
find ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib -type d -name 'tests' -exec rm -rf '{}' +
find ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib -type d -name 'idle_test' -exec rm -rf '{}' +

cd ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/bin
rm -f idle3* 2to3*
rm ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib/libpython3.so

# add dubious python -> python3 link
ln -s python3 ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/bin/python

# Drop site-packages README.txt to avoid SCA dep on python3~3.M
cd ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib/python3.*
rm site-packages/README.txt
rmdir site-packages

rm -R "${{targets.contextdir}}"/usr/lib/python3.*/idlelib

rm -R "${{targets.contextdir}}"/usr/lib/python3.*/ensurepip/_bundled/

find ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib -type f -name '*.pyc' -exec rm -rf '{}' +
find ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib -type f -name '*.pyo' -exec rm -rf '{}' +

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}"
${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/bin/${{vars.python}} -B -m compileall -f --invalidation-mode=unchecked-hash \
    -r100 ${{targets.contextdir}}/usr/lib/

pipeline.name: Remove GUI and documentation files before splitting packages

pipeline.runs:
rt="${{targets.outdir}}/${{package.name}}${{range.key}}-runtime"
mkdir -p ${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/bin ${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/lib
for f in "$rt"/usr/bin/python3.* "$rt"/usr/bin/pydoc3.*; do
  case "$f" in *-config) continue ;; esac
  mv -v "$f" ${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/bin
done
mv -v "$rt"/usr/lib/python3.* ${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/lib
mv -v "$rt"/usr/lib/libpython3.*.so.* ${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/lib

# pyconfig.h is needed at runtime... ugh.
d=$(cd "$rt" && echo usr/include/python3.*)
mkdir -p "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/$d
mv "$rt"/$d/pyconfig.h "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/$d/

# move usr/lib/python3.X/config-3.X-x86_64-linux-gnu
# back into -runtime so the -base-dev can take it below.
d=$(cd "${{targets.subpkgdir}}" && echo usr/lib/python3.*)
mkdir -p "$rt/$d"
mv -v "${{targets.subpkgdir}}/$d"/config-3.* "$rt/$d"

pipeline.name: Verify venv installs expected packages
Build and import a C extension from its directory

pipeline.runs:
# usr/lib/python3.X/config-3.X-x86_64-linux-gnu
# split/dev will only move 2 files from it, but we want all of it.
rt="${{targets.outdir}}/${{package.name}}${{range.key}}-runtime"
d=$(cd "$rt" && echo usr/lib/python3.*)
mkdir -p "${{targets.subpkgdir}}/$d"
mv -v "$rt"/$d/config-3.* "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/$d

pipeline.name: Build and import a C extension from its directory
Verify working python3 -m venv
pipeline.runs:
d=$(mktemp -d)
python3 -m venv "$d"
$d/bin/pip list
$d/bin/pip check
rm -Rf "$d"

pipeline.name: hashlib and hmac refuse unapproved digests in FIPS mode
pipeline.runs:
# Mock FIPS mode the way CPython's own Lib/test/_test_hashlib_fips.py
# does: activate the base provider only, so no digest implementation is
# reachable and every usedforsecurity=True construction must be refused.
# Needs no FIPS provider, so this runs in any environment.
cat > /tmp/fips.cnf <<'CNF'
config_diagnostics = 1
openssl_conf = openssl_init
[openssl_init]
providers = provider_sect
alg_section = algorithm_sect
[provider_sect]
base = base_sect
default = default_sect
[base_sect]
activate = 1
[default_sect]
activate = 1
[algorithm_sect]
default_properties = fips=yes
CNF
OPENSSL_CONF=/tmp/fips.cnf python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib
import hmac
from _hashlib import get_fips_mode

if get_fips_mode() != 1:
    raise SystemExit("FAIL: could not mock FIPS mode")

names = sorted(hashlib.algorithms_available)

# Positive control: the unapproved-service indicator still works, so a
# blanket hashlib breakage cannot pass for FIPS enforcement.
for name in names:
    hashlib.new(name, usedforsecurity=False)

# hmac has no usedforsecurity escape hatch, and 3.14 added a builtin
# HACL* HMAC that would otherwise answer for every digest OpenSSL has
# just refused -- through two separate fallbacks.
for name in names:
    for label, call in (
        ("hashlib.new", lambda n=name: hashlib.new(n, usedforsecurity=True)),
        ("hmac.new", lambda n=name: hmac.new(b"key", b"msg", digestmod=n)),
        ("hmac.digest", lambda n=name: hmac.digest(b"key", b"msg", n)),
    ):
        try:
            call()
        except ValueError:
            continue
        raise SystemExit(f"FAIL: {label}({name!r}) was not refused in FIPS mode")

print("OK:", len(names), "algorithms refused via hashlib.new, hmac.new and hmac.digest")
PY

pipeline.name: Werewolf protections hold, and allowances take each back
pipeline.runs:
chmod 755 /
root_work=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 755 "$root_work"
cat > "$root_work/identity.c" <<'WEREWOLF_IDENTITY_C'
#define _GNU_SOURCE
#include <grp.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 4) return 125;
    uid_t real = (uid_t)strtoul(argv[1], NULL, 10);
    uid_t effective = (uid_t)strtoul(argv[2], NULL, 10);
    if (setgroups(0, NULL) || setresgid(65534, 65534, 65534) ||
        setresuid(real, effective, effective)) {
        perror("identity probe");
        return 125;
    }
    execvp(argv[3], argv + 3);
    perror("identity exec");
    return 125;
}
WEREWOLF_IDENTITY_C
cc -Wall -Werror -o "$root_work/identity" "$root_work/identity.c"
rm -f /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
root_refused() {
    if "$@" >"$root_work/out" 2>"$root_work/err"; then
        echo 'probe: FAIL: effective root ran' >&2; exit 1
    fi
    grep -F 'effective UID 0' "$root_work/err"
    grep -F '"event":"runtime-denial"' "$root_work/err" | grep -F '"group":"root"'
}
root_refused python3 -V

# A real root UID does not prevent execution after effective privileges drop.
"$root_work/identity" 0 65534 python3 -V
# A non-root real UID must not disguise effective root.
root_refused "$root_work/identity" 65534 0 python3 -V
: > "$root_work/target"
ln -s "$root_work/target" /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
root_refused python3 -V
rm /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
mkdir /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
root_refused python3 -V
rmdir /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
mkdir -p /etc/runtime-hardening
: > /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
chmod 600 /etc/runtime-hardening/build-root
python3 -V
rm -rf "$root_work"
echo "probe: ok: python checks effective UID; only the build marker permits root"
mkdir -p /tmp/probe
cat > /tmp/probe/probe.py <<'WEREWOLF_PROBE_PY'
# What this Python lets a program do, as one JSON line; tests/probe.sh compares
# it with what the protections in patches/series and the image's allowances say.
import importlib
import json
import pickle
import site
import sqlite3
import sys


def can_import(name):
    try:
        importlib.import_module(name)
    except ImportError:
        return False
    return True


def can_unpickle():
    blob = pickle.dumps(len)          # a GLOBAL opcode: find_class('builtins', 'len')
    try:
        pickle.loads(blob)
    except Exception:
        return False
    return True


print(json.dumps({
    'ignore_environment': sys.flags.ignore_environment,
    'no_user_site': sys.flags.no_user_site,
    'user_site': bool(site.ENABLE_USER_SITE),
    'sibling': can_import('sibling'),      # beside this script: still on sys.path
    'pythonpath': can_import('pathevil'),  # in PYTHONPATH
    'userbase': can_import('userevil'),    # in PYTHONUSERBASE's site-packages
    'sqlite_extensions': hasattr(sqlite3.Connection, 'enable_load_extension'),
    'native': can_import('ctypes'),        # python:native
    'deserialize': can_unpickle(),         # python:deserialize
}, sort_keys=True))

# Interactive libraries must be absent even when native imports are allowed.
for _module in ('readline', '_curses', '_curses_panel'):
    if __import__('importlib.util', fromlist=['find_spec']).find_spec(_module) is not None:
        raise AssertionError('unexpected terminal extension: ' + _module)
WEREWOLF_PROBE_PY
cat > /tmp/probe/probe.sh <<'WEREWOLF_PROBE_SH'
#!/bin/sh
# probe.sh PROBE: hold the installed python to the protections in patches/series,
# then grant each capability group and see it return. The package test runs it
# as root with /etc/runtime-hardening/allow free to use. PYTHON names another
# interpreter and ALLOW another tree, for a dev build off the read-only root.
set -eu
probe=$1
python=${PYTHON:-python3}
allowdir=${ALLOW:-/etc/runtime-hardening/allow}
base=$allowdir/all/python
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work" "$allowdir"' EXIT

grant() { mkdir -p "$base"; : > "$base/$1"; }
revoke() { rm -f "$base/$1"; }

expect() {
	name=$1; want=$2; shift 2
	got=$("$@" 2>"$work/err") || true
	if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "probe: ok: $name"; return; fi
	echo "probe: FAIL: $name" >&2
	echo "  want $want" >&2
	echo "  got  $got" >&2
	cat "$work/err" >&2
	exit 1
}

refuse() {
	name=$1; token=$2; shift 2
	if "$@" >/dev/null 2>"$work/err"; then
		echo "probe: FAIL: $name ran" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
	if ! grep -q "$token" "$work/err"; then
		echo "probe: FAIL: $name refusal does not name $token" >&2
		cat "$work/err" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
	echo "probe: ok: $name"
}

version=$("$python" -V 2>&1 | cut -d' ' -f2 | cut -d. -f1-2)
mkdir -p "$work/script" "$work/path" "$work/userbase/lib/python$version/site-packages"
cp "$probe" "$work/script/probe.py"
echo 'NAME = "sibling"' > "$work/script/sibling.py"
echo 'VALUE = 1' > "$work/path/pathevil.py"
echo 'VALUE = 1' > "$work/userbase/lib/python$version/site-packages/userevil.py"
echo 'print("script ran")' > "$work/child.py"

report() {
	# PYTHON* are set but must be ignored, so pathevil and userevil stay unseen.
	env PYTHONPATH="$work/path" PYTHONUSERBASE="$work/userbase" "$python" "$work/script/probe.py"
}

# The probe is a script on a writable mount, so running it needs writable-source;
# that is the harness enabler, tested on its own with a child below.
rm -rf "$allowdir"
grant writable-source

closed='{"deserialize": false, "ignore_environment": 1, "native": false, "no_user_site": 1, "pythonpath": false, "sibling": true, "sqlite_extensions": false, "user_site": false, "userbase": false}'
expect 'closed: PYTHON* ignored, user site off, no native or deserialize' "$closed" report
grep -F '"group":"native"' "$work/err" | grep -F '"detail":"_ctypes"'
grep -F '"group":"deserialize"' "$work/err" | grep -F 'builtins.len'

# The fallback unpickler logs too, even with sys.stderr replaced and the
# exception caught. It must use the same native stderr writer.
cat > "$work/pure-pickle.py" <<'PY'
import io, pickle, sys
sys.stderr = io.StringIO()
try:
    pickle._Unpickler(io.BytesIO(pickle.dumps(len))).load()
except pickle.UnpicklingError:
    print('blocked')
PY
expect 'caught pure-Python pickle denial reaches stderr' blocked "$python" "$work/pure-pickle.py"
grep -F '"group":"deserialize"' "$work/err" | grep -F 'builtins.len'

# inline: -c and piped stdin give code, refused unless python:inline.
refuse '-c is refused' python:inline "$python" -c 'print(1)'
refuse 'piped stdin is refused' python:inline sh -c 'echo "print(1)" | "$0"' "$python"
grant inline
expect '-c returns once inline is allowed' '1' "$python" -c 'print(1)'
revoke inline

# writable-source: a script whose file is on a writable mount, refused unless allowed.
revoke writable-source
refuse 'a script on a writable mount is refused' python:writable-source "$python" "$work/child.py"
grant writable-source
expect 'the same script runs once writable-source is allowed' 'script ran' "$python" "$work/child.py"

# native (ctypes) and deserialize (pickle) each return with their group alone.
grant native
expect 'native allows ctypes' "$(printf '%s' "$closed" | sed 's/"native": false/"native": true/')" report
revoke native
grant deserialize
expect 'deserialize allows pickle' "$(printf '%s' "$closed" | sed 's/"deserialize": false/"deserialize": true/')" report
revoke deserialize

# A link is not an allowance, even to a regular file: lock times will be links.
: > "$work/target"
ln -s "$work/target" "$base/native"
expect 'a link is not an allowance' "$closed" report
rm -f "$base/native"

echo "probe: ok: every python protection holds, and each group takes its own back"

# Celery beat uses shelve, often backed by GDBM. Keep persisted schedules readable.
grant deserialize
cat > "$work/schedule.py" <<'PYCODE'
import dbm.gnu
import shelve
import sys
path = sys.argv[1]
with dbm.gnu.open(path, 'c') as raw:
    with shelve.Shelf(raw) as schedule:
        schedule['daily'] = {'task': 'documents.tasks.consume_file', 'runs': 3}
with dbm.gnu.open(path, 'r') as raw:
    with shelve.Shelf(raw) as schedule:
        assert schedule['daily']['runs'] == 3
        assert schedule['daily']['task'] == 'documents.tasks.consume_file'
print('schedule persistence works')
PYCODE
expect 'Celery-style GDBM schedules survive reopening' 'schedule persistence works' "$python" "$work/schedule.py" "$work/schedule"
WEREWOLF_PROBE_SH
sh /tmp/probe/probe.sh /tmp/probe/probe.py
